request.spec:
Backing is now the sum of the patrons' settled figures over their SETTLED claims dated within the
90 days up to and including the sheet's today (each at its frozen figure), 0.00 with none.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Backing is now the sum of the patrons' settled figures over their SETTLED claims dated within the
90 days up to and including the sheet's today (each at its frozen figure), 0.00 with none.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Backing now works the way the request describes, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The change is one component: `PersonBacking` in `src/main/frontend/features/patrons/PersonPatrons.tsx`. A person's backing is now the sum of their patrons' **SETTLED** claims dated in the 90 days up to and including the sheet's today (today minus 89 days, through today). Each claim counts at the figure fixed when it was settled. With no such claims it shows `0.00`. Before, backing added up the patrons' full due-totals.

Because the frozen figure is used, changing a rate later doesn't change backing. The tests check this, along with voiding a claim and moving today forward so claims fall out of the window.

The server and stored data didn't need changes, because the claims the front end already loads include each settled claim's frozen figure. The opening comment in the existing migration `V22__person_patron.sql` still describes the old rule (patrons' due-totals). I left it as it is because migrations that have already run shouldn't be edited.
